A.explanation: Peak height is 2 divisions at $5.0\text{ mV}$ per division giving $10\text{ mV}$, and period of 4 divisions at $5.0\text{ ms}$ per division gives $50\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: Amplitude of $10\text{ mV}$ is correct but $100\text{ Hz}$ would need a period of $10\text{ ms}$, which is only 2 divisions.

C.explanation: Frequency of $50\text{ Hz}$ is correct but $20\text{ mV}$ mistakes peak-to-peak height for amplitude.

D.explanation: Uses full $4$ division vertical extent for amplitude and half the $4$ division period for frequency.

hints: Count vertical divisions from the centre line to a peak for amplitude, not from trough to peak, with Y-gain $5.0\text{ mV}$ per division.
Count horizontal divisions for one complete cycle of the sine wave on the $5.0\text{ ms}$ per division time-base to get the period $T$.
Use $V_0 = \text{divisions} \times \text{Y-gain}$ and $f = 1/T$ with $T$ converted to seconds to check $\text{mV}$ and $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Look at the vertical scale: the centre line is zero and the peak reaches $2$ divisions above it, while the trough reaches $2$ divisions below it.
Amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium, so $V_0 = 2.0 \times 5.0\text{ mV} = 10\text{ mV}$.
Look at the horizontal scale: one full sine cycle repeats every $4$ divisions, for example from one rising zero-crossing to the next.
Period is $T = 4.0 \times 5.0\text{ ms} = 20\text{ ms} = 0.020\text{ s}$, so frequency is $f = 1/T = 1/0.020\text{ s} = 50\text{ Hz}$.
Amplitude $10\text{ mV}$ with frequency $50\text{ Hz}$ matches the table row. This is option A.
